entries.name: DeviceSpecSupport
entries.note: n/a: Apple model-identifier specification tables for Apple hardware: the reference index lists only an Info.plist and version.plist for this framework (no binary, resources or services extracted) and no other bundle in the index references it by name. BifrOSt's own hardware facts are in the About page (sysinfo).

entries.name: DeviceToDeviceManager
entries.note: n/a: Apple's device-to-device link broker. The reference index shows its plug-ins awdl_d2d.bundle and WiFiAwareD2DPlugin.bundle, which bring up AWDL, Apple's proprietary peer-to-peer Wi-Fi link used for AirDrop and Continuity-style device sharing. There is no open equivalent and BifrOSt does not mirror those protocols.

entries.name: DeviceTreeKit
entries.note: Device-tree parsing is done by the Linux kernel and sysfs. BifrOSt has no separate device-tree framework, and the SDK exposes no device-tree API to apps.

entries.name: DiagnosticExtensions
entries.note: n/a: host of sysdiagnose plug-ins. The reference index shows PlugIns/AirPlayDiagnosticExtension.appex, BluetoothDiagnosticExtension.appex and similar, each with 40-odd localisations; they gather logs into an archive for filing with Apple. Diagnostic collection for upload to Apple is not mirrored; BifrOSt logs stay on the machine (bifrost-log, the Console app).

entries.name: DiagnosticExtensionsDaemon
entries.note: n/a: daemon side of the sysdiagnose plug-in host (see DiagnosticExtensions). The reference index lists its awdgen.yaml, Apple's analytics metric definition file, so it feeds Apple analytics and diagnostic archives; BifrOSt sends no telemetry.

entries.name: DiagnosticExtensionsKit
entries.note: n/a: the framework a sysdiagnose diagnostic extension links (sibling of DiagnosticExtensions and DiagnosticExtensionsDaemon). The reference index holds only plists and the signature; the plug-in system it serves collects archives for Apple and is not mirrored.

entries.name: DiagnosticLogCollection
entries.note: Unified logging writes entries to journald, and the store reads them back through the subsystem registry. There is no sysdiagnose-style archive that bundles logs for a support request.
entries.ready_note: Unified logging writes to the journal and reads entries back; tested in bifrost-core log::tests.

entries.name: DiagnosticRequest
entries.note: n/a: client of the Diagnostics and Usage request service (DiagnosticRequestService), which Apple uses to task devices to upload diagnostics. Telemetry and diagnostics upload; BifrOSt has none.

entries.name: DiagnosticRequestService
entries.note: n/a: Apple's diagnostics request service. The reference index lists its Core Data models DRSCKConfigModel.momd (CloudKit configuration), DRSDataModel.momd and DRSTaskingDataModel.momd (server tasking), so it fetches Apple-side tasking over CloudKit and uploads diagnostics. BifrOSt has no Apple account, CloudKit or diagnostics upload.

entries.name: DiagnosticsKit
entries.note: n/a: runs Apple Diagnostics (service hardware tests). The reference index shows com.apple.DiagnosticsKit.XPCTestService.sb (sandbox profile for the test service) and Localizable.loctable. It tests Apple hardware for Apple service flows; BifrOSt PC has generic hardware and no service-diagnostics flow.

entries.name: DiagnosticsSessionAvailability
entries.note: n/a: XPC service DiagnosticsSessionAvailabilityService (58 index entries, all localisations) that decides whether an Apple Diagnostics session may start. Part of the Apple hardware service diagnostics flow; not mirrored.

entries.name: DialogEngine
entries.note: n/a: Siri dialog template catalogs. The reference index holds 5515 entries, mostly Catalog/Templates/dialog/*.catfamily/*.cat files such as siri_errors_serverNotFound_dontCare.cat, Apple-authored response strings for Siri. BifrOSt's assistant writes its own replies (springboard/src/shell/assistant.rs) and cannot reuse Apple's templates.

entries.name: DifferentialPrivacy
entries.note: Adds noise to usage statistics before the reference system's vendor collects them (XPCServices for the collector); the vendor telemetry pipeline has no meaning on this system.

entries.name: DigitalTouchShared
entries.note: Shared drawing and tap messaging for the vendor's own messaging ecosystem across its watch and phone devices; it has no meaning on this system.

entries.name: DirectResource
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal plumbing with no user- or app-visible surface. The reference index holds only Info.plist, version.plist and the code signature (9 entries): no resources, plug-ins, services or localised strings. The exact job is not confirmed from the index, but there is nothing visible to mirror and no other bundle in the index names it.

entries.name: DirectoryEditor
entries.note: Settled ready this wave; see ready_note.
entries.ready_note: Built this wave: a directory server list (Book) with add, remove, rename, enable, search-order moves, validation, persistence, a connection probe through ldapsearch and the OpenLDAP client defaults (URI and BASE lines). Passwords are never stored (the caller passes them from the keychain). It is the model and store behind the editor; no Settings pane draws it yet.

entries.name: DirectoryServer
entries.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/directory_node.rs; springboard/ui/src/directory_query.rs; springboard/ui/src/directory_local.rs; springboard/sdk/src/ldap_directory.rs; springboard/sdk/src/krb5_client.rs; packaging/arch/runtime-packages.txt (openldap, krb5)
entries.note: Settled ready this wave; see ready_note.
entries.ready_note: The reference component is the directory service (opendirectoryd with its Kerberos helper): nodes and records, record queries, the local user and group directory, and remote directories. BifrOSt covers each in code: sessions and nodes (directory_node), queries (directory_query), the local passwd and group tables as records (directory_local), LDAP servers read through ldapsearch (ldap_directory) and the Kerberos client (krb5_client), with openldap and krb5 in the runtime package set. Sign-in still checks only the installer account, a gap tracked on the public OpenDirectory row.

entries.name: DiskImages
entries.note: Create, attach, detach, inspect and convert RAW and ISO disk images through the hdiutil command and the shell's image control socket. Sparse bundles and encrypted images are not covered.
entries.ready_note: RAW and ISO image create, attach, detach, inspect and convert are in bifrost-core, with the hdiutil tool.

entries.name: DiskImages2
entries.note: The same RAW and ISO image model and hdiutil commands cover the basic image path. The second-generation sparse and encrypted image formats are not implemented.
entries.ready_note: The same RAW and ISO image model and hdiutil commands cover the basic image path.

entries.name: DiskManagement
entries.note: Mount, unmount, eject, erase, partition, verify, repair and RAID commands through the disk session and diskutil. Disk arrival and removal events for apps are not provided (see disk-arbitration).
entries.ready_note: Mount, unmount, eject, erase, partition and verify are in bifrost-core, with the diskutil tool.

entries.name: DiskSpaceDiagnostics
entries.note: The low-space level, the notification name and the warning sentence are tested headless in springboard/core/tests/parity_os-gaps-07.rs. Built 2026-10-17: the shell reads /data capacity on every Info and posts the warning through low_space::Watch (once per escalation, then every six hours); tests low_space::watch_tests.
entries.ready_note: The low-space level, the warning sentence and the once-per-escalation Watch are tested headless; the shell reads capacity on each Info and posts through it.

entries.name: DisplayServices
entries.note: Reads and sets the panel brightness from the backlight class, with a maximum. It does not cover display colour, rotation or multi-display configuration.
entries.ready_note: Panel brightness is read and set through the backlight class; tested in bare::power.

entries.name: DisplayTransportServices
entries.note: n/a: the index shows DisplayTransportServicesAgent.xpc, the agent that manages Apple's display transport links (external displays over USB-C, Thunderbolt and DisplayPort tunnelling on Apple hardware). On Arch the kernel DRM and typec drivers do this and BifrOSt's compositor only consumes the connectors, so there is no BifrOSt-owned layer.

entries.name: DistributedEvaluation
entries.note: Evaluates the vendor assistant's models across the vendor's own devices. It serves the vendor ecosystem, and BifrOSt ships no cross-device model service.

entries.name: DistributedSensing
entries.note: n/a: multi-device sensing between a user's Apple devices; the index holds only plists plus a FeatureFlags/Domain/DistributedSensing.plist. Apple device-ecosystem feature with no open equivalent.

entries.name: DistributedTimers
entries.note: n/a: keeps timers in step across a user's Apple devices (iPhone, Watch, HomePod) over the Apple account and its device transport. BifrOSt timers are local to the Clock app; no Apple account or ecosystem transport exists. The index holds only plists.

entries.name: DistributedTimersDaemon
entries.note: n/a: daemon of DistributedTimers, which syncs timers across a user's Apple devices over the Apple account. No Apple account or device ecosystem in BifrOSt; the index holds only plists and the signature.

entries.name: DoNotDisturb
entries.note: Focus on and off is built: it silences banners and screen wakes, keeps notifications, and persists, as tested in focus.rs. No Shortcuts or voice intent toggles it yet.
entries.ready_note: Focus on and off, with the state the shell persists, is built in the shell and tested in shell::focus.

entries.name: DoNotDisturbKit
entries.note: The shell's focus accessors (dnd, set_dnd) hold the state a client would read. No app-facing kit is exposed through the SDK yet.
entries.ready_note: The shell's focus accessors hold the state a client reads; tested in shell::focus.

entries.name: DoNotDisturbServer
entries.note: Quiet hours and the persisted focus state are built in the shell. The reference server's settings model and cross-device settings sync are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: Quiet-hours schedule and persisted focus state are in the shell; tested in shell::notify::schedule.

entries.name: DocumentCamera
entries.note: A camera document scanner that reaches the desktop only through a bridge bundle (the glue bundle DocumentCameraAppKitGlue) built for the tablet UI. BifrOSt scans through its own print and scan page, so the bridge has no job here.

entries.name: DocumentUnderstanding
entries.note: Ships the vendor's trained language model assets (embedding files, tokenizer vocabulary, factor tables) for its own document analysis features. BifrOSt ships none of these models.

entries.name: DocumentUnderstandingClient
entries.note: Client of the vendor's document analysis service, which runs on the vendor's own model assets. BifrOSt ships none of these models, so the client has no job.

entries.name: DoubleAgent
entries.note: Kernel upcall daemon for the vendor's own filesystem implementation. Linux filesystem drivers and FUSE do this job without a daemon of this kind.

entries.name: DrawingBoard
entries.note: A tablet-only drawing board framework (its Info.plist marks it for tablet devices only). BifrOSt's desktop drawing uses the Freeform canvas, so a tablet drawing surface has no job on the desktop.

entries.name: DrawingKit
entries.note: Stroke painting into a pixel canvas for Freeform is built and tested in ink.rs. The reference paint shaders (wet paint, dry composite, paper texture) are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: Stroke painting into a pixel canvas for Freeform is built and tested in ink.

entries.name: Drift
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal service. The index shows the framework is only plists, with a separate ExtensionKit extension System/Library/ExtensionKit/Extensions/Drift.appex; tools/parity/os_inventory.py already classes it as an Apple internal service. No BifrOSt equivalent is wanted.

entries.name: DuetActivityScheduler
entries.note: Partial: the background service (services/background.rs) runs deferred app tasks gated by network and external power. Not built: idle-state gating, system jobs beyond app tasks, and systemd timers as the scheduler.
entries.ready_note: The background service schedules deferred app work; tested in shell::services::background.

entries.name: Dyld
entries.note: The Apple dynamic linker framework. On Arch, ld.so and glibc do the linking and apps are native ELF, so the framework is not an SDK surface.

entries.name: DynamicPrefetching
entries.bifrost: springboard/core/src/launch_prefetch.rs; springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (note_launch at app launch); springboard/src/bin/shell.rs (warm_default worker at start-up)
entries.note: Settled ready this wave; see ready_note.
entries.ready_note: Built this wave: the shell records each app launch (id, executable, time) in a local state file, ranks apps by recency-weighted frequency with a bonus for the same hour of the day, and at start-up reads the executables of the top four within a 256 MB budget so the first launch finds them in the page cache. Local only, no telemetry. Tests cover ranking, hour wrap, ageing, bounds, text round trip, warm budget and persistence.

entries.name: EAFirmwareUpdater
entries.note: n/a: firmware updates for External Accessory (MFi) devices over Apple's accessory protocol. Apple-licensed accessory firmware with no open equivalent; the index holds Info.plist and an en.lproj only.

entries.name: EAP8021X
entries.note: PEAP and TTLS with MSCHAPv2 are configured through wpa_supplicant in wifi_config.rs. EAP-TLS and certificate-based 802.1X are not built, and the reference trust-store helper has no counterpart.
entries.ready_note: PEAP and TTLS with MSCHAPv2 are configured through wpa_supplicant; tested in net::wifi_config.

entries.name: EDPSecurity
entries.note: n/a: enterprise data protection for managed (MDM) devices, by its name and the reference Info.plist (the only content in the index). BifrOSt has no MDM or managed-device mode, so there is no policy to enforce.

entries.name: EFILogin
entries.note: Builds the firmware login screen resources (efires bitmaps and the EFI resource builder) for the vendor's boot firmware. BifrOSt boots through systemd-boot and ukify, so this firmware login screen has no job.

entries.name: EXDisplayPipe
entries.note: n/a: Apple silicon display pipeline support; the index shows the matching kernel extensions EXDisplayPipeH17P.kext and EXDisplayPipeH18G.kext for Apple SoC generations. Apple hardware internals; BifrOSt PC drives Intel/AMD/NVIDIA display hardware through the Linux DRM drivers.

entries.name: EXSurface
entries.note: n/a: same EX family as EXDisplayPipe (Apple silicon display and surface plumbing); the index holds only plists and the signature. Apple SoC internals; Linux DRM provides the surfaces BifrOSt uses.

entries.name: EasyConfig
entries.note: n/a: Apple's wireless accessory configuration (onboarding an accessory onto Wi-Fi), by its name and Info.plist, the only content in the index. Apple-only accessory protocol; BifrOSt has none.

entries.name: Ecosystem
entries.note: Daemons for the vendor's accessory ecosystem (ecosystemd and ecosystemagent, with curated accessory display names and assets). BifrOSt pairs no vendor accessories through this path.

entries.name: EcosystemAnalytics
entries.note: Analysis daemon that inspects Mach-O binaries and sends analysis events to the vendor, with a local ignore list (ecosystemanalyticsd). That is vendor telemetry, and BifrOSt does not upload it.

entries.name: EcosystemUI
entries.note: n/a: prompts and strings for Apple device-ecosystem features such as pairing and Continuity (51 index entries, almost all localisations, no code). The ecosystem it fronts is an Apple-only protocol and account feature BifrOSt does not mirror.

entries.name: EfiSupport
entries.note: n/a: Apple Mac EFI firmware update support (the index holds only plists). BifrOSt PC is a generic UEFI Arch machine whose boot loader the installer writes; Mac firmware images do not apply.

entries.name: ElementRegistry
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal registry of ecosystem elements shared with the iOS family (a tablet copy of its Info.plist and an iOSSupport sibling of ElementRegistryClient are in the index). It has no resources, plug-ins or strings and no user-visible surface to mirror.

entries.name: ElementRegistryClient
entries.note: n/a: client of the Apple-internal ElementRegistry; the index lists both a macOS copy and System/iOSSupport/.../ElementRegistryClient.framework, i.e. iOS-family sharing code. Only plists and the signature; nothing user-visible.

entries.name: ElementRegistryFoundation
entries.note: n/a: foundation layer of the Apple-internal ElementRegistry (see ElementRegistry and ElementRegistryClient). The index holds only Info.plist, version.plist and the signature; no user-visible surface.

entries.name: EligibilityQuorum
entries.note: n/a: Apple's per-account and per-region feature eligibility check, by its name and Info.plist (the only index content). Account and store gating for Apple-hosted features; BifrOSt has no Apple account.

entries.name: Email
entries.note: Mail account setup and storage are built in the Mail app: accounts are loaded, added and updated, and the setup form builds the IMAP and SMTP settings. System-wide account provisioning and the reference configuration plist are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: Mail account loading, adding and updating, and the setup form that builds the IMAP and SMTP settings are tested in accounts::tests. System-wide account provisioning is still missing, so the row stays partial.

entries.name: EmailAddressing
entries.note: Sender parsing and address matching are built and tested in the Mail app. Address completion for other apps is not built.
entries.ready_note: Sender parsing (person_from), address matching (has_address) and the person record are built in the Mail app and tested in people::tests. Address completion for other apps is not built, so the row stays partial.

entries.name: EmailCore
entries.note: MIME attachment stripping and the message model are built in the Mail app. The reference attribution, currency and subject-prefix pattern tables are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: MIME attachment stripping and the message model are in the Mail app; tested in mime.

entries.name: EmailDaemon
entries.note: Mailbox sync over IMAP runs inside the Mail app process. There is no separate mail daemon, and the reference cloud mirroring model is not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: Mailbox sync over IMAP runs in the Mail app process and is covered by springboard/apps/mail-desktop/src/imap.rs host tests. The reference cloud mirroring model is not built and is not part of the main job. Verify on Midget.

entries.name: EmailFoundation
entries.note: Mail parses MIME parts and speaks IMAP in these two files. There is no shared email surface for other apps and no SMTP send path in them.
entries.ready_note: Mail parses MIME parts in the Mail app; tested in mime.

entries.name: EmbeddedAcousticRecognition
entries.note: Settled ready this wave; see ready_note.
entries.ready_note: The reference component is the embedded (on-device) acoustic speech recogniser behind dictation and Siri. BifrOSt's on-device recogniser is the whisper pipeline (ui whisper), the SDK recogniser and its whisper backend, and the consent-gated shell recogniser service; the same code covers the public Speech rows. It needs the model download and is not yet verified on Midget.

entries.name: EmbeddedOSSupportHost
entries.note: n/a: host driver support for Apple's embedded-OS coprocessors (T2 and bridge-style chips). The index shows the kernel extension AppleEmbeddedOSSupportHost.kext that references this framework. Apple hardware; BifrOSt PC has no such coprocessor.

entries.name: EmbeddingCore
entries.note: Built: hashed bag-of-words embeddings and cosine ranking in the SDK (embedding::EmbeddingIndex, 256 dims, FNV-1a with sign bit). Added in slice g4: bifrost_ui::semantic_hash::HashedSemantic, a SemanticHook over words plus character trigrams (512 dims, diacritic and case folded via the search tokenizer, bounded text length), wired as the semantic reranker of the Spotlight Documents source (quicksearch::indexed_groups). Not a neural model: no learned weights and no synonyms; word forms (run, running) are close through trigrams. App and settings search results still use NoSemantic; the ranker scores only items that already hold a query word, so recall is unchanged.
entries.ready_note: Document search results are reordered by a local hashed-text similarity (semantic_hash::tests prove word-form closeness, folding, caching and that the hook only raises scores of matching items). The SDK keeps the app-side EmbeddingIndex (embedding::tests). A learned embedding model is not bundled.

entries.name: EmbeddingService
entries.note: The SDK has a word-vector table with nearest-neighbour and distance queries (embedding.rs) and a table of named models that serves requests (ml_runtime.rs), tested in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-complete-25.rs. Gap: no shell service hosts embedding models for search, and the vectors come from the caller rather than from a bundled model.
entries.ready_note: The word-vector table with nearest-neighbour and distance queries is in bifrost-ui; tested in embedding.

entries.name: EmojiFoundation
entries.note: The keyboard emoji page has categories, a recently used list and search state. Per-language keyword tables are not built.
entries.ready_note: The keyboard emoji page has categories, recents and search; tested in emoji.

entries.name: EncoreXPCService
entries.note: Siri assistant XPC service (bundle identifier in the Siri namespace); the binary was not extracted. Apple assistant services are not part of BifrOSt.

entries.name: Engram
entries.note: n/a: a Core Data store (Model.momd, Model.mom in the index) for on-device personal-context learning that feeds Apple's suggestion and intelligence features, in the same family as CoreDuet (already n/a). It has no meaning without Apple's suggestion services, which BifrOSt does not run. The model schema itself was not read.

entries.name: EnhancedLinkSecurityStore
entries.note: n/a: Apple-internal store for link security state, by its name and Info.plist (the only index content). No resources, plug-ins or strings and nothing user-visible; BifrOSt link and TLS security is handled by the Linux stack and rustls.

entries.name: EnhancedLogging
entries.note: Opt-in detailed diagnostic logging that is sent to the reference vendor's analytics pipeline. BifrOSt keeps its diagnostics local, so the component has no job here.

entries.name: EnhancedLoggingState
entries.note: Holds the opt-in state of the detailed diagnostic logging that is sent to the reference vendor. Without that upload it has no job.

entries.name: Ensemble
entries.note: n/a: a single binary with no resources plus a FeatureFlags/Domain/Ensemble.plist feature-flag domain in the index; an Apple feature-flagged multi-device component. No user-visible surface or open equivalent; the exact job is not confirmed from the index.

entries.name: EntityService
entries.note: Apple intelligence entity service (bundle identifier in the intelligence namespace); the binary was not extracted. Apple assistant services are not part of BifrOSt.

entries.name: Eryx
entries.note: n/a: the index shows a 712 KB default.metallib; the shader row for it is already n/a as machine-learning image processing. BifrOSt has no on-device model pipeline and ships no Apple ML models.

entries.name: Espresso
entries.note: A pure-Rust CPU evaluator runs chains of dense, relu and softmax layers and reads models from their text form (ml_model.rs), behind the named model table in ml_runtime.rs. Gap: there are no convolution or recurrent layers, no binary model package format and no compute device path.
entries.ready_note: A pure-Rust CPU evaluator runs dense, relu and softmax layer chains; tested in ml_model.

entries.name: EventKitExternalSync
entries.note: CalDAV account sync for Calendar runs through this sync type when the Calendars service is on. Other external calendar sources and iCal sync schemas are not built.
entries.ready_note: CalDAV account sync for Calendars runs through springboard/sdk/src/dav_sync.rs and is covered by its host tests. Other external calendar sources are outside this framework's main job. Host tests only; verify on Midget.

entries.name: EventKitUICore
entries.note: Calendar's event form pickers and its quick event sheet cover event entry. There is no shared event-editing UI kit for other apps.
entries.ready_note: Calendar's event form pickers and quick event sheet (pickers.rs, quickentry.rs) are covered by their host tests. No shared event-editing kit for other apps is a gap. Verify on Midget.

entries.name: EventMetaDataExtractor
entries.note: The data detector finds calendar dates in plain text, in yyyy-mm-dd and d.m.yyyy forms (detect.rs). Gap: no code reads the title, time, place or end of an event from a message, and calendar-desktop offers no event suggestions.
entries.ready_note: The data detector finds calendar dates in plain text; tested in detect.

entries.name: ExchangeNotes
entries.note: Not applicable: this is the notes source for a proprietary server protocol, and BifrOSt's account layer syncs only over CalDAV and CardDAV (springboard/sdk/src/dav_sync.rs), so there is no account source to build it on.

entries.name: ExchangeSync
entries.note: Not applicable: the sync engine for a proprietary server protocol is outside BifrOSt's account design. Account sync covers CalDAV and CardDAV only (springboard/sdk/src/dav_sync.rs).

entries.name: ExchangeSyncExpress
entries.note: Not applicable: the lightweight sync path belongs to the same proprietary server protocol as the account sync engine, which BifrOSt does not carry. Its counterpart for account sync is CalDAV and CardDAV (springboard/sdk/src/dav_sync.rs).

entries.name: ExchangeWebServices
entries.note: Not applicable: this client speaks a proprietary SOAP-over-HTTPS server protocol that BifrOSt's account layer does not implement. Account sync uses CalDAV and CardDAV (springboard/sdk/src/dav_sync.rs).

entries.name: ExclaveFDRDecode
entries.note: Decodes fault records from the vendor's secure-world enclave on the vendor's own silicon. BifrOSt has no such hardware.

entries.name: ExclaveSISPTestServices
entries.note: Test services for the vendor's secure-world partition, used on factory and lab hardware only.

entries.name: ExclavesMessageQueueProducer
entries.note: Producer side of the message queue into the vendor's secure-world enclave. The enclave exists only on the vendor's silicon.

entries.name: ExclavesMessageQueueTypes
entries.note: Message type definitions for the vendor's secure-world enclave queues. They have no meaning without that enclave.

entries.name: ExclavesOutboxConsumer
entries.note: Reads outbound messages from the vendor's secure-world enclave. The enclave exists only on the vendor's silicon.

entries.name: ExclavesOutboxListener
entries.note: Listens for outbound messages from the vendor's secure-world enclave. The enclave exists only on the vendor's silicon.

entries.name: ExclavesStats
entries.note: Statistics for the vendor's secure-world enclave. The enclave exists only on the vendor's silicon.

entries.name: ExpansionSlotSupport
entries.note: Support for the vendor's expansion-slot modules and their helper service on desktop hardware BifrOSt does not target.

entries.name: ExposureNotificationDaemon
entries.note: Bluetooth exposure notification service that public health regions run through the vendor's region bundles and servers. BifrOSt has no counterpart.

entries.name: ExtensionKitSettings
entries.note: Settled ready this wave; see ready_note.
entries.ready_note: The reference framework is the Login Items and Extensions pane that lists app extensions and background agents and lets the user turn them on or off. BifrOSt has that page: it reads extension and background-agent tables from installed manifests, builds the Settings groups, stores the off lists in preferences and filters runnable agents (shell::login_items_page::tests).

entries.name: FATCommon
entries.note: n/a: no user- or app-visible function to mirror. The reference index lists only an Info.plist for this library bundle (no resources, XPC service, plug-in or host bundle), so its job could not be identified; nothing in BifrOSt depends on it and no open equivalent is claimed.

entries.name: FMCore
entries.note: Find My location and device-finding core. It talks to the vendor's Find My network and servers, which BifrOSt does not run.

entries.name: FMCoreLite
entries.note: Lightweight Find My core. It serves the vendor's Find My network and servers, which BifrOSt does not run.

entries.name: FMCoreUI
entries.note: Find My user interface with map views of the vendor's Find My network. It has no meaning without that service.

entries.name: FMF
entries.note: Find My location sharing over the vendor's servers. BifrOSt does not run that service.

entries.name: FMFCore
entries.note: Follower location sharing and its shared-location records are served by the vendor's account cloud; BifrOSt runs no such account service, so nothing here needs building.

entries.name: FMFUI
entries.note: The interface for follower location sharing needs the vendor's account cloud and has no BifrOSt counterpart.

entries.name: FMIPCore
entries.note: Remote lock and erase of devices run through the vendor's account service, whose records and accounts are cloud-side; BifrOSt has no such service.

entries.name: FMNetworking
entries.note: Find My location-network transport. Inferred from the name; the reference holds only the binary's plists and a string table. BifrOSt has no Apple account or Find My network.

entries.name: FRC
entries.note: n/a: the reference frame-rate conversion runs trained neural optical-flow networks from Apple's ML model packs, which cannot be reproduced clean-room. BifrOSt uses ffmpeg's motion-compensated minterpolate filter (bifrost field); output quality differs.

entries.name: FTAWD
entries.note: n/a: FaceTime wireless-diagnostics helper. FaceTime is a proprietary Apple call protocol and the diagnostics part uploads telemetry to Apple; the index shows only localized string tables (about forty lproj folders) and a plist. BifrOSt mirrors neither.

entries.name: FTClientServices
entries.note: The client side of the vendor's video calling service depends on that vendor's cloud accounts and call routing; BifrOSt ships no such service.

entries.name: FTServices
entries.note: Backend service plumbing for the vendor's video calling cloud; BifrOSt has no such service and no call routing to provide.

entries.name: FWAVC
entries.note: n/a: FireWire (IEEE 1394) AV/C device control. The index holds only Info.plist and version.plist. FireWire is a legacy bus that no BifrOSt target (PC x86_64, tablet aarch64) is built around; a PC with a FireWire port is served by the Linux firewire stack, which BifrOSt does not wrap.

entries.name: FaceTimeDockSupport
entries.note: private framework, owner n/a: FaceTime conferencing

entries.name: FaceTimeFeatureControl
entries.note: private framework, owner n/a: FaceTime conferencing

entries.name: FaceTimeMacHelperCore

entries.name: FinderSyncPriv
entries.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/file_manager_sync.rs; springboard/sdk/src/fswatch.rs; springboard/sdk/src/file_coordination.rs; springboard/apps/files/src/extensions.rs; springboard/src/shell/apphost.rs; springboard/src/shell/extension_host.rs; springboard/ui/src/extension_manifest.rs
entries.note: private framework, owner FinderSync; from SDK matrix finder-sync.json Built 2026-10-17 (wave 12): file-manager sync extension model in springboard/sdk/src/file_manager_sync.rs (tests file_manager_sync::tests). Wired 2026-10-17 (wave 14): Files hosts the extension apps that declare file_manager_folders and draws their badges and menu rows (extensions.rs). Launch on demand 2026-10-17: the declaration makes the app an extension of the system point is.bifrost.file-manager-sync, and Files reaches it through the shared extension host (extension_host.rs), which starts it in extension mode when one of its folders is shown and stops it when idle; the app no longer has to be running (the menu never waits for a launch and shows its rows from the next menu). Host tests only, not run on Midget; no Settings enable screen, toolbar button not drawn.
entries.ready_note: An app whose manifest.toml has file_manager_folders = ["~/Cloud"] is an extension of the system point is.bifrost.file-manager-sync for those folders. Files finds it at start, but the shared extension host starts it (in extension mode, running SyncService) only when one of its folders is shown, and stops it after 30 s idle; the app does not have to be running. Files tells it which folder is shown, asks it for badges on a worker thread (drawn on icon, list and column items on the next frame) and for menu rows when a shortcut menu opens (the menu never waits for a launch: an extension that is not running is started in the background and shows its rows from the next menu), and sends the chosen row back, only for paths inside the declared folders. The toolbar button it can describe is not drawn and Settings has no enable screen. Tested with an in-process extension launched and reaped by a real host over real sockets; verify with an extension app on Midget.

FontManager registers installed and app-supplied faces and matches a FontSpec (fontobj), the user's font choice is kept per role (fontprefs, UserFonts), unknown family names resolve to open equivalents by class with a fallback cascade (font_substitution), and the Font Book app lists and validates the library. entries.name: FoundInAppsPlugins

Built 2026-10-17: bifrost-core search_merge joins hits from several providers round-robin with per-provider and total caps (tests search_merge::tests). Open: no app-side provider call yet.
entries.ready_note: The job is showing items that apps hold in the system search. Apps index their own items (sdk quicksearch), the shell's search index lists them under Documents and opens them in the app (spotindex), and results from several providers merge round-robin with per-provider and total caps (core search_merge). Open: an app-side provider call so an app answers a query from its own search code.

entries.name: FoundationODR
entries.note: private framework, owner Foundation; from SDK matrix foundation-app-support.json, foundation-files-persistence.json, foundation-fundamentals.json, foundation-networking-lowlevel.json Built 2026-10-17: OperationQueue on worker threads (sdk operation_queue, tests operation_queue::tests). Built 2026-10-17 (wave 12): on-demand resources in springboard/sdk/src/on_demand_resources.rs (tests on_demand_resources::tests). Open: the App Store fetch.
entries.ready_note: Built 2026-10-17: on-demand resources. A Catalog names tagged payloads (size, SHA-256, preservation priority); a ResourceStore fetches missing tags through a caller-supplied fetch, verifies and installs them atomically (background_download::stage), pins them for the life of a ResourceRequest (begin, conditionally begin, end accessing, progress) and purges unpinned tags under a disk budget, lowest preservation priority and least recently used first (on_demand_resources tests). Open: wiring a fetch to the PC App Store, and loading-priority scheduling.

entries.name: FrontBoard
entries.note: The shell starts apps over a socket pair, holds each app's newest presented surface and gives every app its own resource ownership. Built 2026-10-17: scene model in bifrost-core scene_set (several scenes per app, saved state restored by id; tests scene_set::tests). Open: not wired into the app host yet.
entries.ready_note: The scene and process host: the shell starts apps and holds their presented surfaces (apphost, app_manager), the `scenes` shell service opens, lists, focuses, reopens and closes an app's scene windows (scene_services), the scene model keeps per-scene saved state restored by id (core scene_set), and apps receive the session lifecycle in order (sdk scene_session).
